E1.stem: Explain why language models split text into tokens instead of reading whole words or single characters.
E1.answer: Tokens are a middle ground. A fixed vocabulary of whole words cannot cover rare or new words, while single characters make sequences very long and hard to model. Sub-word tokens keep the vocabulary small, still cover any word by combining pieces, and keep sequences short enough for the model to process.
rubric: a whole-word vocabulary cannot cover rare or new words
sub-word tokens give a small vocabulary and short sequences

E2.stem: What does self-attention let a model do that a plain left-to-right reading of the words does not?
E2.answer: Self-attention lets every token look at every other token in the sequence and weigh how relevant each one is. The model can therefore connect words that are far apart, such as a pronoun and its noun, and it can process all positions in parallel instead of one at a time.
rubric: every token can look at every other token
weights say how relevant each token is
links distant words such as a pronoun and its noun

E3.stem: Why does a RAG system retrieve text before answering instead of relying on the model's memory alone?
E3.answer: Retrieval gives the model the relevant passages at question time. Answers can use up-to-date or private documents the model never saw in training, they can cite their sources, and the model is less likely to invent facts.
rubric: supplies relevant passages at question time
covers recent or private documents missing from training
allows citing sources and reduces made-up facts

P1.stem: A model has a context window of 4,096 tokens. A prompt uses 1,500 tokens and the answer is limited to 500 tokens. How many tokens are still free in the window? Show the steps.

P2.stem: A vector search returns the 3 passages nearest to a question. Their cosine similarities are 0.82, 0.64 and 0.91. Which passage should rank first, and which one is the weakest match? Explain.
P2.answer: Higher cosine similarity means a closer match, so rank by descending score: 0.91 first, then 0.82, then 0.64. The 0.91 passage ranks first and the 0.64 passage is the weakest.
rubric: higher cosine similarity means a closer match
